steps.text: Heat oil in a large skillet over high heat. Add garlic; cook and stir until fragrant, about 1 minute. Sprinkle red pepper flakes and paprika into the oil; add shrimp and toss to coat. Pour in lemon juice; allow to cook until the shrimp are bright pink on the outside and the meat is no longer transparent in the center, 1 to 2 minutes more. Reduce heat to medium-low; add basil and toss lightly. Season with salt and pepper to serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Spicy Garlic Shrimp
raw_recipe.description: Spicy garlic shrimp is easy to make with pan-fried shrimp, garlic, red pepper flakes, lemon juice, and basil for a quick, flavorsome meal in minutes.

review.reviewBody: SO easy. I used the frozen cooked shrimp to make it even easier. I thawed them and removed the tails then heated them up in the saute pan with red pepper flakes, cayenne pepper, salt, olive oil, garlic and lemon juice. Really good with some veggies and rice.

I cooked the garlic on a lower heat than suggested, thanks to reminders from other reviewers. I used frozen uncooked shrimp from trader Joe's, defrosted, then removed the tails. I added butter to the oil up front and didn't have any paprika but it turned out great! 

I served it over wild rice and can't get over how beautiful it looks. I posted a photo. Because it makes me look like I know what I'm doing. Which I so do not. 

This is definitely going to be all up in the rotation.

Easy and delicious! I halved since it was to pair with our steaks (surf and turf!) dinner tonight. Since I halved - and used a even smidge less oil, mixed all together and treated like a marinade. Let the mixture sit on the shrimp about 20 min before cooking stir-fry style on our Blackstone. The red pepper flakes add some zip but still was tolerable even for my husband who is heat sensitive. I could see this great on a salad! Or orzo as another reviewer mentioned. But, it was great as is! Thanks REBECCADK! Great recipe! Will make more times this summer!

The recipe is great. I did make a few changes. I only had 1 pound of shrimp so I cut up a pound of tilapia (recommeded by another reviewer) and cooked with it. I also added 1 cup of chopped portabella mushrooms and sauted with the garlic. It was great and my husband and three boys loved it. Its delicious and so quick and easy to make. We had it with saffron rice and steamed broccoli.

This was awesome, the fiance and I both loved it. Some extra water went into my pan while adding the shrimp, so I ended up removing the shrimp when they were done cooking and reducing the residual broth (and adding a little flour) to make it a thicker sauce for the shrimp. It was great over rice pilaf!

This is an awesome recipe! I made it for Fathers Day and my gourmet cook husband loved it as did my teenage daughter. I halved the recipe for the three of us using a 12 Oz. bag of raw unpeeled jumbo shrimp. The only changes I made was to double the amount of garlic (for the half recipe, 3 big cloves) and also the amount of fresh basil. I also added 2 tablespoons of butter to the olive oil. I served it over linguine with butter, along with a green salad and a crusty baguette. Delicious!

for being so simple this dish was really tasty.. i cut the recipe in half and used a lot less oil (trying to cut calories) and upped the garlic to 2 cloves.. i only had dried basil and bottled lemon but this still came out really good! cut down on the red pepper flakes (my stomach has been temperamental lately) and eyeballed the salt.. i'll be making this again and again.. ty so much for the recipe

Spices were a great combo for the Shrimp. I stir-fried zucchini, yellow squash , onion, red and green pepper in olive oil and lightly used seasoned salt. Stirred in with pasta and put the shrimp on top. I wouldn't change a thing with the shrimp recipe itself. Thank you for sharing!

Wonderful! 
sorry I did not make as is. Did not have basil so used cilantro based on the nature of the ingredients and it was superb. Thank you again. Served over chuka soba noodles and tossed with the shrimp before serving. This is the second time I have made this and will make it many more.
This shrimp was delicious! My aunt helped me and we threw about a half cup of white wine on the shrimp after the lemon juice, and they tasted even better!!

This was a quick meal to prepare for a week-night supper. I added onion, carrots and celery to the garlic and mixed the finished dish with penne pasta. Will be adding this one to my permanent collection
We had these spicy shrimp over fettuccine for a delicious meal. Good amount of heat.
Super easy and great for a hot night with a salad. Update 4/14/2024: I left out the salt this time and we didn’t miss it! One of my favorite recipes!
Less red pepper, more lemon and basil. Serve on orzo.
Easy and delicious. Can’t beat that. Only sub I made was to 1/2 the pepper. Served it over a green salad with roasted potatoes.
I enjoyed this. I was surprised that someone found it bland. Unless I accidentally switched the red pepper flakes with the paprika, it was pretty spicy. I also added spinach to it.

It was easy, simple to cook. I cut back on the shrimp by one pound as well as the ingredients. I added less red peppers and lemon juice and I add Twist noodles instead of having rice for the sauce. The dish was delicious to eat.
Made this for dinner tonight and everyone thought it was delicious. We used fettuccine . Otherwise didn't change anything. Yum!
Great dish. So easy to make and tastes great. I used frozen shrimp and I added fresh lemon juice (4 lemons). Love it! Will definitely make it again.
